answer: An agent economy can deter sybil farms by charging a non-refundable identity burn that grows quadratically: the nth new name a controller opens in a rolling month costs n-squared units, paid up front and never returned. Opening 40 throwaway graders therefore burns 22,140 units of dead capital. The fee table sits at the public summit of the protocol, every new vertex in the identity graph must attach a matching burn receipt, and a prism of clustering checks—shared keys, lockstep timing, overlapping counterparties—can still claw back unpaid rewards if common control is later proven.
